haiku-low.q1: MySQL commits the write with its outbox row, then inline-syncs to Postgres with a 250 ms timeout. A Postgres failure is logged and swallowed; the user still gets success.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the existing Postgres row is not a tombstone (deleted_at is NULL) and the incoming version is higher than the stored version.
haiku-low.q3: Every running instance shows dual_mysql with no old-code instance left, the outbox is healthy, and replica lag is 5 seconds or less. Instances can disagree for up to 30 seconds.
haiku-low.q4: It reads the MySQL replica in batches of 2000, checks replica lag before every batch and sleeps while it is above 5 seconds, and throttles itself to protect Postgres.
haiku-low.q5: Reads: a zero-mismatch comparison pass, then ramping the percentage to 100 and holding 3 days. Source switch: 3+ days at 100%, a clean comparison, outbox under 5 seconds old, Postgres healthy.
haiku-low.q6: The outbox row, written in the same MySQL transaction, records the need to copy. The repair worker retries forever with backoff capped at 60 seconds; backfill and comparison also repair.
haiku-low.q7: A MySQL copy takes a FOR SHARE lock on users_erased and skips erased ids. Postgres upserts never overwrite tombstones, which are kept permanently.
haiku-low.q8: Progress is last_id in Postgres migration_state, committed in the same transaction as each batch, with a lease allowing one runner. It stops when an empty batch meets the lag condition and sets done.
haiku-low.q9: The comparison job checks every id and column in both tables. Persistent differences are rechecked, pushed into the current source-of-truth outbox for repair, and recorded in migration_state.
haiku-low.q10: Every instance is paused and idle with zero in-flight writes before the source changes, so none writes elsewhere. If the wait misses its deadline, the flag goes back to dual_mysql, keeping the pause under 90 seconds.
haiku-low.q11: After the switch, Postgres assigns ids via users_id_seq. At each source change the incoming counter is set to the largest id in either database plus 1,000,000, so ids stay unique, including after rollback.
haiku-low.q12: Reverse dual writes keep MySQL current. Rollback pauses, drains the outbox, sets MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT past the largest id, then sets dual_mysql. The option ends when pg_only is set, after 14 days.

sonnet.q1: MySQL is written first (commit with an outbox row in the same transaction), then after commit an inline sync copies the user's current row to Postgres (250 ms timeout). If the Postgres part fails, the failure is logged and swallowed; the caller still sees success, and the outbox row stays for the repair worker.
sonnet.q2: Only if the existing Postgres row is not a tombstone (deleted_at IS NULL) and its version is lower than the incoming version (users.version < EXCLUDED.version). A missing row is simply inserted.
sonnet.q3: app_flag_value must be dual_mysql on every running instance (series count equals the orchestrator's instance count, no old-code instance remains); the outbox must be healthy; mysql_replica_lag_seconds must be 5 or less. Instances can disagree for up to 30 seconds after a flag change (30-second cache refresh).
sonnet.q4: It reads from the MySQL replica (not the primary) in batches of 2000 (WHERE id > last_id ORDER BY id), checks mysql_replica_lag_seconds before every batch and sleeps while it is above 5. It also throttles itself to protect Postgres. NOT STATED beyond that for MySQL load.
sonnet.q5: Reads: step 6 comparison has had one complete pass with zero persistent mismatches (backfill done first). Source of truth: reads at 100% on Postgres for at least 3 days with zero persistent mismatches, latest comparison clean, oldest outbox row under 5 seconds old, Postgres healthy, and scrape interval for app_flag_value and users_writes_inflight 10 seconds or less.
sonnet.q6: The outbox row (users_sync_outbox), written in the same transaction as the write, records it. While MySQL is the source of truth it lives in the MySQL primary (forward outbox). The standalone repair worker polls it (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) and syncs the user to Postgres, retrying forever with backoff capped at 60 seconds; backfill and comparison also repair gaps.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones: a delete writes a Postgres tombstone (deleted_at set) unconditionally, even if the row was never copied. The guarded upsert (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND version lower) never overwrites a tombstone and is atomic on the primary key, so a stale copy cannot recreate the user. (Into MySQL, users_erased with FOR SHARE does the same.)
sonnet.q8: In the Postgres table migration_state (last_id checkpoint, done flag, plus a lease row allowing a single runner). Each batch is one Postgres transaction that upserts the rows and sets last_id to the batch's highest id, so the checkpoint moves only with committed data. It stops when an empty batch occurs with the lag condition met, which sets done.
sonnet.q9: The full comparison job scans every id in both tables, comparing all columns including version and checking for Postgres rows with no MySQL counterpart. A difference is rechecked against the MySQL primary and Postgres once nothing is pending in the outbox for that id; only a persistent difference counts as a mismatch, and it is pushed into the outbox of the current source of truth for repair. Results are kept in migration_state.
sonnet.q10: A paused write mode: every instance returns a retryable 503 for writes and touches no database. The operator waits until all instances show paused with users_writes_inflight 0 (by T0+45) and the MySQL outbox is empty (by T0+55), sets the sequence, then sets dual_pg. Pause is at most about 85-90 seconds. If a wait misses its deadline, or an outbox row is stuck, set the flag back to dual_mysql (instances resume within 30 s, pause under 90 s, nothing has moved).
sonnet.q11: Postgres assigns ids via users_id_seq in dual_pg and pg_only, copying them to MySQL as explicit ids. At the switch, inside the pause, setval is set to the MySQL primary's max id + 1,000,000. On rollback, MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT is set to (largest id in Postgres or MySQL) + 1,000,000 before returning to dual_mysql.
sonnet.q12: In dual_pg, writes commit to Postgres with an outbox row there (reverse outbox), then are copied to MySQL; the worker repairs misses, and the comparison runs daily. Rollback: set paused, wait for all instances paused and in-flight 0, drain the Postgres outbox to 0, set MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT, set dual_mysql (same 90-second budget). The option ends when users_write_mode is set to pg_only (step 12), allowed after at least 14 days with clean comparison and outbox.
